textbook.definition: A book used for learning a subject.

journal.definition: A publication containing research articles in a particular academic field.

database.definition: An organized body of related information.

search-engine.definition: A service that finds webpages matching words that you type into a search box.
search-engine.exampleUsage: She used a search engine to locate relevant research pages.

bibliography.definition: A list of writings with time and place of publication (such as the writings of a single author or the works referred to in preparing a document etc.).

citation.definition: A short note recognizing a source of information or of a quoted passage.

footnote.definition: A printed note placed below the text on a printed page.

index.definition: An alphabetical list of topics and the pages where they appear in a book.

abstract.definition: A short summary of a research paper's purpose, methods, and main findings.

peer-review.definition: Evaluation of research by other specialists before or after publication.

essay.definition: A piece of writing that develops an argument or discusses a subject.

thesis.definition: A substantial research document submitted for an academic degree; the specific qualification varies between education systems.

dissertation.definition: A substantial research document submitted for an academic degree; universities differ in their use of this term.

paper.definition: A written academic article or assignment about a particular subject.

report.definition: A written document describing the findings of some individual or group.

literature-review.definition: A scholarly paper or section that examines and connects published studies about a particular subject.

methodology.definition: The approach and methods used to carry out a study.

conclusion.definition: The closing section of academic writing that brings together its findings, argument, or implications.

introduction.definition: The opening part of a report or study that presents its topic.

appendix.definition: Supplementary material that is collected and appended at the back of a book.

note-taking.definition: Writing down important information while reading, listening, or studying.

flashcard.definition: A study card with a question or word on one side and information on the other.

mind-map.definition: A diagram that connects related ideas around a central topic.

outline.definition: A plan showing the main points and structure of a piece of writing.

highlight.definition: To mark important words or passages so they are easy to notice.

summarize.definition: To give the main points of something in a shorter form.

review.definition: To study material again or examine it carefully.

memorize.definition: To learn something so that it can be recalled later.

practice-test.definition: A sample examination used to prepare for a real test.

study-group.definition: A small, casual gathering lets students prepare together after class. Members exchange notes, explain difficult ideas, and review what they have learned.

plagiarism.definition: Presenting another person's words or ideas as your own without proper acknowledgment.

reference.definition: Details identifying a source used in academic work.

original-work.definition: A book, artwork, or other creation made by its named author or artist rather than reproduced from another person's work.
original-work.exampleUsage: The paper distinguished the student’s original work from properly attributed sources.

paraphrase.definition: To restate another source’s meaning in your own words while giving appropriate acknowledgment.

quote.definition: To repeat words spoken or written by someone else.

source.definition: A person, document, or place that provides information.

academic-honesty.definition: The principle of completing academic work truthfully, giving proper credit, and avoiding cheating, fabrication, or plagiarism.
academic-honesty.exampleUsage: The course begins with a discussion of academic honesty.

turnitin.definition: An educational software service that can report text similarity and support assignment workflows; a similarity score alone does not determine plagiarism.
turnitin.exampleUsage: The university uses Turnitin as part of its academic-integrity process.

honor-code.definition: A school's official policy sets standards for student behavior, with special attention to honesty in assignments and exams.
